study.title: Acts 18 The Gospel in Corinth and the service of Apollo in Ephesus
study.overview: Acts 18 shows Paul coming to Corinth after the experience in Athens, working with Aquila and Priscilla, preaching in the synagogue and seeing opposition, but also conversions and direct encouragement of the Lord. The chapter highlights the advancement of the gospel amid rejection, divine protection over the mission and the importance of well-founded biblical teaching. Then the text follows the continuity of Paul's journey and presents Apollos, a skilled but still incomplete preacher in his understanding, which is instructed more accurately and becomes very useful to believers.

outline.title: Paul in Corinth: work, preaching and rejection
outline.explanation: Paul arrives in Corinth, works with Aquila and Priscilla in the same office and preaches weekly in the synagogue. When Silas and Timothy arrive, he dedicates himself even more intensely to the testimony that Jesus is the Christ. The resistance of the Jews leads Paul to declare that he would now turn to the Gentiles.

outline.title: Fruit of the Lord's preaching and protection
outline.explanation: Paul proceeds to teach in the house of Justus, and Crispus, his house and many Corinthians believe and are baptized. The Lord encourages you in vision, promising presence, protection and a people prepared in that city. The attempt to bring him to court fails when Gallio refuses to judge an internal dispute over words and the Law.

outline.title: Return and strengthening of churches
outline.explanation: Paul remains even more time in Corinth, aside to Syria, passes through Ephesus, visits Jerusalem and returns to Antioch. Then he travels through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening the disciples, showing that his mission was not only to start churches, but also to consolidate them.

outline.title: Apollo: Zeal, instruction, and defense of Scripture
outline.explanation: Apollos comes to Ephesus already knowing the Scriptures and teaching correctly about the Lord, although he knew only the baptism of John. Aquila and Priscilla guide you more accurately. As he goes to Achaia, he becomes of great help to believers and publicly demonstrates through the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.

study.context: Corinth appears in the text as an important and influential city of the province of Achaia. The notes also describe their negative moral fame and their business weight. The chapter also mentions Claudius' command to expel Jews from Rome, and quotes Gallius as proconsul of Achaia, situating Paul's conflict within the Roman world. Ephesus emerges as an expressive center of teaching and debate, where Apollo is active.
study.theology: The chapter teaches that the Christian mission advances by the combination of daily work, public preaching, patient teaching and the direction of the Spirit. Paul does not separate spiritual vocation from manual labor, and this highlights the dignity of common service when dedicated to God. Human opposition does not nullify the divine promise; on the contrary, the Lord strengthens the messenger with presence, protection, and certainty that there are people prepared to hear. It is also seen that the truth of the gospel must be confirmed by the Scriptures and communicated clearly. Apollos exemplifies zeal and capacity, but also the need for humble correction and more complete teaching. Thus, the chapter presents a church that grows through the Word, mutual encouragement and cooperation between different servants.

scholarViews.insight: The notes highlight that Aquila and Priscilla were a prominent couple in the early church and who worked as tentmakers, as well as Paul.
The comment notes that Paul changed his synagogue to Justus' house when he was prevented from following at the Jewish meeting, using a new opportunity to continue preaching.
The note states that Paul stayed in Corinth for a prolonged period, teaching and receiving the providential protection of God when the Lord assured him that no one would harm him.

questions: How does Paul unite daily work and spiritual service without separating one thing from the other?
What does the promise of the Lord in Corinth teach about perseverance in the midst of opposition?
How does Aquila and Priscilla's attitude with Apollo show the importance of teaching more accurately without humiliating who already believes and serves?
study.practice: This chapter calls the reader to remain faithful when there is rejection, trusting that God sustains his work and opens doors where there was previously resistance. It also teaches to value careful biblical teaching, hospitality to God's servants, and cooperation in ministry. In practice, it is worth examining whether our faith produces perseverance, humility to be corrected and willingness to explain the Scriptures clearly to others.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided allow you to safely state only what is explicitly mentioned in them. There is not enough basis in them to detail exact chronologies beyond what the chapter itself and the comments indicate. It is also not possible to define with certainty, from these notes, all the internal motives of Paul in each shift; some readings are interpretive inferences, not facts narrated explicitly.
